title: A viewer's frame pool becomes its own struct
body:
`Viewer` in `compositor.rs` has seventeen fields, and seven of them belong to the buffer pool: `formats`, `formats_due`, `linear`, `pool`, `next_buffer`, `ready` and `wants_frame`. `render_to`, about 105 lines, first finds or allocates a slot and announces it with `ServerMessage::Buffer`, then renders into it and sends `Frame`. The rule "drop a slot whose size is stale once it is not lent out, and send `Forget`" is written twice: in the `Release` arm of `viewer_message` for slots that come back stale, and in `forget_stale` for idle slots at a resize.

`Gpu::allocate_linear` in `gpu.rs` is `Gpu::allocate` with an empty format list, since `allocate` already falls back to `Xrgb8888` with the linear modifier when nothing matches. The compositor's `|| viewer.formats.is_empty()` branch picks between the two.

## Proposal

A `Pool` struct on `Viewer` with `slot(size, gpu) -> Option<usize>`, `release(id, size)` and `forget_stale(size)`, so the stale rule has one home and `render_to` keeps only rendering and sending, about 30 lines. `allocate_linear` goes and the call becomes `allocate(w, h, if viewer.linear { &[] } else { &viewer.formats })`.
